d: Two-lane activation in a marked grid: players move in single file up one side, round the end cones and back. Use for progressive mobility and running drills (high knees, skips, lateral shuffles) before increasing pace.

Three-lane speed warm-up from the end line: lane 1 through a speed ladder into a sprint, lane 2 over mini-hurdles/poles, lane 3 a straight-line acceleration. Groups rotate lanes; focus on foot contacts and posture before sprinting out.
Four-lane line warm-up: small groups jog up and back in parallel lanes between cones. Simple dynamic stretching and movement-prep progression for a full squad.
Mixed-movement warm-up in a central grid with two teams (bibs) intermingling, while individuals run a loop around the outside cone. Free movement and agility in traffic with progressive intensity.

Adaptation warm-up around a rectangle of cones: players work through three lanes with straight runs and changes of direction, then curve back around the outside. Low-to-moderate intensity movement patterns to re-adapt players to running loads.
Three-lane linear conditioning: players start behind mini-hurdles and sprint the full length to a cone. Repeated straight-line runs with walk-back recovery.

Two-station circuit (A and B): station A combines a curved run, ladder footwork and a short sprint; station B adds a dribble and a figure-of-eight around a pole. Players rotate between stations; mixes agility, acceleration and ball work.
Three-lane warm-up between mannequins: players run from the start line to a mid-grid mannequin and on to the far one. Progressive build-up of running speed with a turn at the end.
Variation of the three-lane mannequin warm-up with angled runs between the two mannequin lines. Builds running speed and introduces direction changes at controlled intensity.
Long linear runs across the pitch between cones/poles, three groups working in parallel. Extensive running (out and back) for aerobic conditioning or tempo work.

Three-lane warm-up with different starts: lane A from a speed ladder, lane B with lateral steps, lane C from a ground/rotational start, then all sprint to the far mannequin. Varied starting positions to prepare for acceleration.
Slalom warm-up: players weave a curving path through mannequins up the grid after a lateral shuffle at the start. Agility, footwork and change of direction at warm-up intensity.
Three-lane acceleration warm-up (A, B, C) with short reactive starts from ladder/cones before a straight sprint to the end mannequin. Prepares for maximal acceleration.
Three straight lanes running from the start line to a mannequin halfway up the grid. Short acceleration runs, building intensity with each repetition.
Reaction sprints from the penalty area: players line up in rows and sprint out across the cones on a coach's cue. Reaction speed and acceleration with the full squad.
Cross-shaped reaction drill with four start points (A–D): players react and sprint to the centre, with variations including a dribble or a turn. Reaction, acceleration and change of direction.
Reaction game in two small zones: pairs respond to a signal to chase or escape towards cone gates. Competitive reaction-speed work in a compact area.
Full-pitch lap: the squad runs around the perimeter of the pitch from the halfway line. Use as a general warm-up jog or an aerobic running block.

Grid of small squares with a defender (black) in each central square and attackers (red) dribbling around the outside. Attackers keep the ball while moving through the grid; warm-up with a light pressure element.
Three-lane resistance and movement circuit: lane A ladder and line hops, lane B over mini-hurdles, lane C a weaving dribble/run around poles. Players rotate lanes; coordination and acceleration.
Mixed-station warm-up around the grid: A agility around mannequins, B ladder footwork into a run over hurdles and markers. Coordination, footwork and short accelerations.
Three-lane warm-up with hurdles, ladder and a weaving run between mannequins, finishing with a sprint out to the end cones. Players rotate through A, B and C.
Two partner drills at the edge of the box: (1) pass, receive and turn away; (2) pass and run onto a return ball in behind. Short passing patterns with movement to prepare for possession work.
Two-stage partner warm-up: (1) a straight run to a cone; (2) players shuttle across the grid with passes to partners at each end. Combines running with short passing.
Circle warm-up: players run from the edge of the circle to collect a ball from the centre (C) and dribble back out. Ball pick-up with changes of direction and acceleration.
Four narrow lanes with players dribbling up and back (A) or working in pairs (B). Close ball control with turns at each end under light intensity.
Partner shuttle from opposite ends (A and B): run, receive and turn back, while line C does a straight run the full length. Combines ball work with linear running.
Diagonal passing and running pattern across a 4-box grid: pass, follow and dribble to the next station (A → B → C). Passing accuracy and movement at warm-up intensity.
Centre-circle passing warm-up from four corner groups: players pass into the circle and follow their pass to the next cone. Continuous passing and running in rotation.
End-to-end passing and running pattern between three groups (A, B, C): pass, overlap and receive back. Combination play and timing of runs.
Two sets of three lanes: one side runs straight through mini-goals/cones, the other runs curved paths. Players rotate start positions (A, B, C); linear and curvilinear running.
Three lanes with mannequins and short hurdles/ladders before a run to the end cone. Players work A–C, combining footwork with acceleration.
Three-lane circuit: A line hops into a sprint, B over mini-hurdles, C weaving around poles. Repeat of the coordination/acceleration lane set-up.
Three acceleration lanes (A, B, C) with different starts (ladder, hurdle, weaving around mannequins), plus a separate 35m straight sprint lane (D). Builds to maximal speed.
Three-lane grid sprints (A, B, C) from the start line to marked cones, with a ladder start in lane B. Progressive accelerations.
Six-box grid with players running out and back in three lanes (A, B, C) between cones. Short repeated shuttles for acceleration and deceleration.

Six-box grid with three lanes (A, B, C): players run to a cone, change direction and return via a different line, with a separate cone pattern (D) at the far end. Short curved runs and turns to prepare for change of direction.
Two-lane warm-up: lane A is a straight acceleration from a low start, lane B a curved run around cones with sharp cuts. Linear vs. multidirectional running in parallel.
Six parallel lanes (A–F): A and B curved runs and slaloms, C a straight run with markers, D–F weaving dribbles with the ball. Players rotate lanes; agility and close control at warm-up intensity.
Penalty-box running drill: groups run out from the side of the box and curve back (A, B, C), while line D runs the full width across the box. Straight and curved runs with short recovery.
Four lanes with two stages: jog to the middle cone then accelerate to the end. Simple progressive acceleration work for a full squad.
Four pairs of lanes inside a zone: partners run and pass up and down their channel. Paired running with short passing to raise intensity.
Centre-circle shuttle relays between two groups: players run through gates and around cones and back to the line. Short shuttles with turns for agility and deceleration.
Four lanes with players running up and down between cone pairs. Extended warm-up runs, progressing tempo each repetition.
Six lanes from the end line: players run straight up and back from a cone. Warm-up strides building speed through repetitions.
Two halves with players running the length of the grid between cones, alternating forward and backward runs and side shuffles. Multidirectional movement prep.
Four lanes across a grid with players starting from the end cones and running to the far line. Basic acceleration runs.
Two parallel channels: one with ladder footwork into a sprint and a passing lane, the other weaving around mannequins. Players alternate; coordination into acceleration.
Speed station with ladders, mini-hurdles and an acceleration zone (marked cones), plus a cone circuit (A–D). Footwork drills feeding into a short acceleration.
Speed-ladder and hurdle footwork in a grid, finishing with an acceleration out to a cone. Two groups (red and black) rotate through the stations.
Two speed stations: A ladder footwork into a run to a cone, B ladder into mini-hurdles. Coordination and quick feet before acceleration.
Four start points (A–D) around a rectangle: A and B straight runs, C a slalom around poles, D a separate goalkeeper/fourth group. Rotating acceleration and agility work.
Circle drill: players with balls around the edge dribble into the centre and back out. Close control and changes of direction in a busy space.
Reactive change of direction: player receives a pass from a partner then cuts left or right to a cone. Reactive agility with a decision.
Two-zone speed set-up: a 5m dynamic zone (low-intensity movement drills) then a 5m acceleration zone through mini-ladders to the far line. Progress from movement prep to acceleration.
Box circuit: players work through ladder sections with sharp turns between them and loop back to the start. Footwork, deceleration and re-acceleration.
Passing square pattern between three groups (A, B, C): pass, follow and dribble to the next cone. Passing and receiving with movement at warm-up intensity.
Three lanes with different starts: A short ladder footwork, B straight acceleration, C ladder into a sprint. Players then sprint to the end line.
Paired dribbling across a grid: players dribble from opposite ends, cross in the middle and take the ball back. Control, turning and spatial awareness.
Six-box grid where players dribble across, beat a cone and turn back out, with groups at each corner. Dribbling with changes of direction and turns.
Three lanes: A weaving around cones, B a straight run, C ladder footwork into a curved run. Rotating agility, acceleration and coordination.
Variation of the corner dribbling grid: players dribble in, turn around a central cone and exit to the next corner. Ball manipulation with changes of direction.
Three lanes (A, B, C): A ladder into a sprint, B straight acceleration, C ladder with a lateral step and turn before the run. Acceleration from varied starts.
Two mirrored passing patterns (A and B): pass forward, then curve the run around a cone to receive or rejoin. Passing combined with curved runs.
Three-group pattern across a grid (A, B, C): long pass from A, dribble around mannequins from B, and a combination at C. Rotating passing and dribbling drill.
Square passing circuit between four corners marked by poles: pass and follow around the square in sequence. Continuous passing and moving.
Three lanes (A, B, C): A straight acceleration, B over mini-hurdles, C ladder with a cut and sprint. Players rotate through.
Two triangle passing patterns (A, B, C): pass, follow and change positions. Short passing and movement at moderate intensity.
Four lanes (A–D): A ladder/footwork start, B a marked acceleration zone, C over mini-hurdles, D a weaving run around cones. Mixed speed stations.
Four lanes in marked strips: D a straight sprint, C over mini-hurdles, B a weaving run, A ladder into a sprint. Players rotate.
Four lanes (A–D): A ladder and turn into sprint, B lateral side shuffles, C over hurdles, D curved slalom. Mixed coordination and speed set.
Four lanes (A–D): A ladder with a turn then sprint, B ladders spaced up the lane, C over hurdles, D a weaving run around poles. Mixed footwork into acceleration.
Four lanes (A–D): A ladder into a sprint, B and D short run-throughs, C over mini-hurdles into a sprint. Speed prep from different start actions.
Four lanes (A–D): A hurdles with a turn, B over spaced hurdles, C a curved run, D a straight sprint through markers. Rotating coordination and acceleration.
Four lanes (A–D) to a cone halfway: A ladder into a slalom, B a zig-zag around markers, C straight over hurdles, D ladder with a turn. Short agility-focused accelerations.
Four lanes (A–D) to a mid-grid cone: A ladder footwork, B a box pattern with lateral steps, C over hurdles, D ladder with a curved cut. Footwork and short change-of-direction runs.
Four lanes through a two-box grid: hurdles, ladders with a turn, poles and ladders before running through to the far line. Coordination stations into acceleration.
Two lanes in a zone: one straight run over low hurdles, one curving run through a hurdle set with cuts. Linear versus curvilinear speed work.
Four lanes of mixed footwork (hurdles, ladders, poles) with the far lane using lateral shuffles between hurdle sets. Players run back down the outside to repeat.
Three lanes (A, B, C): A a curved dribble, B a slalom around cones, C weaving through mannequins, each finishing with a run to the end cone. Agility and ball control.
Four-corner grid (A–D): different movements along each diagonal and side, including slaloms, hurdle hops and long straight runs. Rotating multi-directional warm-up.
Three lanes (A, B, C): A a slalom around cones, B a straight run, C weaving through poles. Players run from the start line to the end cone.
Three-group pattern (A, B, C) with passing between lines and curved runs around the grid. Combined passing and movement in rotation.
Grid with three groups: A dribble up and back around cones, B and C run diagonal and straight shuttle lines. Mixed ball work and running.
Three strips (A, B, C): A and B passing up and down a channel, C with passes into a defender (black) area. Paired passing progressing to opposed receipt.
Three lanes (A, B, C): A straight dribble/run, B and C wide weaving runs around cones to the end line. Curved running and agility.
Four boxes (A–D) with dribbling and passing between them: dribble in, pass across and follow. Passing combination drill with movement.
Three lanes with left/right cones: players run up, choose a side cone (L or R), turn and run on to the mannequin. Change of direction with a decision.
Four lanes (A–D): A curved slalom, B dribble to a mannequin, C over hurdles, D curved run around poles. Rotating agility and acceleration.
Lane warm-up with several start groups: straight runs, curved runs and out-and-back sprints between cones. Progressive running variety.
Three-station circuit: A ladder and bounds/hurdles, B and C sharp runs around mannequins. Coordination and change-of-direction strength.
Grid circuit with hurdles, mannequins and poles: players weave, cut and accelerate through the stations before running out to the far cones.
Three lanes from the edge of the box to cones near halfway: A run with a turn, B a straight run, C a weaving run. Repeated accelerations over 20–30m.
Box-edge conditioning with three lines (A, B, C): A over mini-hurdles into a sprint, B a straight run with a pass, C a dribble across. Mixed running and ball work for moderate conditioning.
Square-and-loop run: players work around a small square of cones then run a long loop out to cone B and back. Aerobic running with direction changes.
Grid with two groups: A runs straight lines the length of the grid, B runs curved diagonal paths across it. Linear and curved running at controlled intensity.
Reaction drill: player from line 1 reacts to a cue and sprints to cone A or B, while line 2 feeds the ball. Reaction and acceleration with ball involvement.
Centre-circle reaction pairs: attacker reacts to the coach and sprints to one of the cones 6m away, chased by a defender. Short reactive sprints in pairs.
Two groups facing each other across ladders: on a cue players sprint to a gate, with one chasing. Reaction and chase/escape sprints.
Straight-line chase: one player starts just behind another and chases them down the line between poles. Competitive linear sprint.
Pairs: a server passes and the receiving player reacts to cone A or B, with a defender in support. Reactive receive-and-go with change of direction.
Two groups racing across the grid: sprint from the start line over ladders/hurdles to the far cones. Competitive linear acceleration.
Diagonal reaction sprint: player dribbles in, then reacts to a cue and cuts left or right through cone gates. Reactive change of direction with the ball.
Two lanes: player runs through ladders, then reacts left or right (L/R) around a mannequin, with a feeder playing the ball. Reactive agility.
Two reaction channels where players dribble around mannequins and then race to finish, opposed by black players. Reactive dribbling under light pressure.
Four groups facing inwards: on a signal players run to the central cones, react and race to the poles. Reactive multi-directional sprints.
Two triangle patterns: pass across, then react and sprint to the cone indicated. Passing combined with reactive accelerations.
Reaction start: player receives a pass, then reacts and sprints left (red ladder) or right (blue ladder) to the cone. Decision-making and acceleration.
Two-line reaction race (A and B): players react to a cue, skip through ladders and race on a curved path to the same far cone. Competitive reaction and curved acceleration.
Two channels (A and B): player comes through ladders, receives from a feeder and reacts to a cone direction, with a defender in one channel. Reactive acceleration after receiving.
Reaction star: player comes off ladders into the centre (A), then reacts to the coach and sprints to one of several cones. Three groups work in parallel boxes.
Left/right reaction: players come off ladders and react to the coach's call (L or R) before sprinting to a cone. Reactive change of direction.
Four-way reaction cross: groups come through ladders from each side towards the centre, then react and sprint diagonally out to corner cones. Multi-directional reactive sprints.
Two mirrored reaction drills: player comes off ladders, a feeder passes, and the player reacts to sprint to one of two cones. Decision-making under time pressure.
Three boxes with groups reacting from a central cone to curved runs out to different cones on a cue. Reactive curved accelerations.
Two pairs of channels: red players race black players up and down the grid in head-to-head sprints. Competitive linear speed.
Head-to-head race: players come through ladders and race to the end line to win a ball against an opponent. Reaction and competitive acceleration.
Zone race: players run a curving course through ladders and markers to the far cone and back. Agility and acceleration in a competitive format.
Three lanes: player dribbles forward, then reacts to a cue and cuts left (blue ladder) or right (red ladder) before sprinting out. Reactive dribbling and acceleration.
Grid with two ladder stations; on a cue a player sprints on a curved path to a far cone and back to the line. Reaction into a longer curved sprint.
Reaction runs from opposite sides: players move into the grid and react with sharp cuts to cones. Short reactive multi-directional efforts.

Timed dribble track around the penalty area (A–I): 10m sprint, dribble through 2m-spaced cones, zig-zag sprints across the area and a backwards run to finish. Repeated-sprint/anaerobic test or conditioning circuit.
Full-pitch fartlek around the perimeter: sprint along the sides, jog the middle sections and walk the short ends. Classic intermittent aerobic run.
Full-pitch interval running: sprint the box edges, stride the diagonals and jog the touchline sections. Aerobic intervals with varied speeds.
Large conditioning circuit (A–H) around half a pitch, combining sprints, dribbles, shots and recovery runs through cones and mannequins. High-intensity station work.
Penalty-area circuit with hurdles, ladders and mannequins linked by sprints and passes. Players rotate around the stations; mixed anaerobic conditioning.
Three-station box circuit (A, B, C): ladder footwork into a sprint and pass, a run round a mannequin, and a curved run back. High-intensity repeated efforts.
Diagonal sprint and finish: player runs the slalom, receives and drives at goal while defenders recover. Speed with ball and shooting under fatigue.
Half-pitch shuttle runs between the box and halfway line, combined with passing at the top of the box. Repeated high-speed runs with ball involvement.
Box-width conditioning: players hop over hurdles at the sides, then sprint across the box between pole gates. Repeated short sprints with plyometric elements.
Simple linear sprint grid: one lane at 10m, one at 20m, from a standing start. Acceleration repeats or speed testing.
Pass and sprint: player passes into the grid then sprints from A to B, followed by a curved recovery run back to C. Repeated sprints with recovery runs.
Three groups (1, 2, 3) in the half: repeated shuttle runs forward and back to cones at different distances. Repeated-sprint ability.
Half-pitch transition sprints: pairs pass, then sprint the width of the pitch (A to B) and back. Repeated sprints with a ball trigger.
Pattern in a grid: player passes, sprints from A to B, loops around a mannequin and finishes to D. High-intensity repeated efforts with ball involvement.
Four-corner box sprints: players hop through hurdles, then sprint across the box to the opposite side. Repeated high-intensity runs with plyometric starts.
Pitch-length shuttles: player sprints from the centre circle into the box, receives/finishes, then sprints back. Repeated efforts with a finish.
Centre-circle patterns from four corners (A–D): curved runs, passing and dribbling into and out of the circle. Continuous high-intensity circuit.
Four lines start at the box edge: react to a cue, curve to a cone and sprint to the halfway line mannequins. Reactive repeated sprints over longer distance.
Four lanes (A–D) from the edge of the box: straight sprint, sprint over hurdles, weaving run and pass-and-go. Mixed repeated sprints.
Penalty-area circuit (A–F): curved runs, overlaps, passes and dribbles around the box. High-intensity conditioning with the ball.
Box circuit (A–E): dribble through cones, pass, then long sprints out to halfway and back. Repeated sprints with technical actions.
Four-corner pattern in the half (A–D): passes, dribbles and runs crossing through the centre. Continuous high-intensity running with ball work.
Five lanes from halfway: players run curved paths (left or right) up to the box, then finish into mini-goals. Repeated high-speed curved runs with a finish.

Four-corner diamond (A–D) with an active-recovery zone in the middle: players run diagonal efforts in and out from each corner, recovering with light passing in the centre. Intermittent work:rest conditioning.
Large cross-shaped running pattern: players sprint long straight lines across and along the area from start points A, B and C. Long high-speed runs for extensive conditioning.
Half-pitch circuit (A, B): players run patterns from the box to halfway, with dribbles and passes through cone gates. Repeated high-intensity efforts with ball work.
Two lines from halfway: pass and react, then sprint 30–40m to cones at the edge of the box (A and B). Repeated longer sprints.
Penalty-box width runs: players dribble or run across the box from side groups (A to B). Repeated efforts with and without the ball.
Full-pitch running pattern (A–F) combining long curved runs, passes and dribbles from box to box. Extensive high-speed running with ball involvement.
Centre-circle patterns from four corners (A–D): curved runs and loops with passes into and out of the circle. Continuous moderate-to-high intensity work.
Half-pitch passing and running circuit between two goals, with mannequins, dribbles and finishing. Conditioning combined with technical actions.
Large half-pitch circuit (A–D) with ladders, mannequins, passes and finishes on goal. High-intensity running with technical demands.
Width-of-pitch circuit with ladders, poles and passing at stations along both touchlines. Repeated efforts mixing footwork, sprinting and passing.
Full-pitch perimeter circuit with ladders, hurdles and passing through midfield. Long intermittent running with varied stations.
Full-pitch pattern play with mannequins: players pass and make overlapping and curved runs from defence to goal. Conditioning through pattern play.
Two goals with goalkeepers: players run crossing diagonal paths and finish, with the ball fed from the sides. Repeated high-intensity efforts with finishing.
2v2 conditioning game in the box: players sprint through ladders to start, play 2v2 to goal, then make recovery runs back. High intensity with transitions.
Pitch-length crossing runs: players sprint diagonal X patterns between the two boxes. Long high-speed running.
Box-edge circuit: players pass into small zones, run around cones and sprint back along the touchline. Mixed-intensity conditioning loop.
Full-pitch width runs: players dribble through cones, pass and sprint the length of the pitch in several lanes, with defenders passing back. Extensive repeated sprints.
Variation of the full-pitch lanes: dribble, pass and long sprints across the pitch with servers in the middle. High-volume repeated running.
Box circuit: pass, run around poles, receive a long ball and finish on goal. High-intensity efforts with crossing and finishing.
Two channels: players come through ladders, then sprint diagonally to a cone, chased by player C. Competitive acceleration.
Reaction and finishing near the box: player reacts to the coach's call (L or R), sprints to a cone, then finishes. Speed with decision-making.
Two grids: player receives from a partner, turns and sprints to cone A or B. Reactive acceleration after receiving.
Reaction pairs across a grid: players come off ladders, react to a cue and sprint to one of the cones. Short reactive efforts.
Two lines facing each other: players dribble forward, pass across and swap lines. Speed of play with the ball.
Four-group pattern crossing in the centre (A to B): curved dribbles and passes past mannequins. Agility and speed with ball.
Player sprints from the start to two different cones, receiving a pass at each, with mannequins in the middle. Change of direction with ball involvement.
Two boxes (A–D): players come through ladders, change direction and accelerate to different cones. Acceleration off a cut.
Edge-of-box circuit: player passes, runs through poles and around mannequins, then sprints across. Repeated efforts with ball work.
Box: player sprints forward through a ladder while two partners feed passes from the sides. Acceleration with receiving.
Four-station grid: players come through ladders, react to a cue and sprint off while defenders chase. Reactive acceleration and competition.
Grid with paired players: sprint out, walk back as recovery, then repeat. Short sprint intervals with walking recovery.
Two lanes: player passes off a mannequin and sprints back (one curves around). Acceleration with a pass trigger.
Player receives from a partner, turns around a central cone and sprints diagonally to a corner. Change of direction after receiving.
Two lanes: player sprints to a mannequin, then reacts to a defender and cuts to one of two poles. Reactive change of direction.
Player sprints forward to a mannequin, receives a pass, then cuts diagonally to one of two cones. Change of direction after receiving.
Player comes through a ladder, receives a pass and accelerates to one of two angled gates. Acceleration after receiving with a choice.
Player comes off a ladder, receives a pass and accelerates to one of two angled gates. Acceleration with a choice after receiving.
Three lanes: players react to a cue (!) from a start line or ladder and sprint to the far cone. Reactive linear acceleration.
Three lanes: player reacts to a visual or ball cue (!) at the start, then sprints the full length. Reaction and maximal acceleration.
Four lanes: short straight sprints from the start line to the halfway cones. Short acceleration repeats.
Central start among mannequins: players sprint diagonally out to the corners of the grid. Multi-directional acceleration.
Two lanes: reaction start (!) from ladders, then a sprint to the far cone. Reactive acceleration over a longer distance.
Two lanes: players come off a ladder, curve around a mannequin and sprint forward. Change of direction into acceleration.
Two lines facing each other: players race and curve around to the same central gate. Competitive curved sprint.
Four lanes (A–C): walk-in start then a straight or curved sprint up the lane. Rolling-start sprints with walking recovery.
Three lanes: short sprints from the start line to the first cone line. Short acceleration repeats.
Three lanes: straight sprints from the end line to cones halfway up. Acceleration repeats.
Four lanes (A, B): walk in diagonally then sprint straight up the lane. Rolling-start accelerations with walking recovery.
Four lanes: player starts from a mannequin/marker and sprints to a cone. Short accelerations.
Passing and sprinting pattern around mannequins: pass, follow and sprint to the next position. Speed with ball involvement.
Four lanes: player receives a short pass at the start, then sprints to the cone. Acceleration with a pass trigger.
Lateral shuffle along the base line between hurdles (A, B), then a sprint forward to a mannequin (C). Lateral movement into forward acceleration.
Long channel: players run through hurdles and ladders, then curve around and sprint back. Coordination and longer speed efforts.
Box: player sprints along the side, then diagonally across the area. Change of direction and acceleration.
Two-sided drill: players come over hurdles towards the middle, receive from a coach, then sprint to the end cone. Footwork into acceleration with ball cue.
Two groups: players come over low hurdles, turn 90 degrees and sprint forward. Footwork into a cut and acceleration.
Box: players start among mannequins, then sprint on curved paths out to the corners. Curved acceleration.
Grid: players start at the top, then make short passes and sprints between cones in pairs. Strength-endurance with short efforts.
Station circuit (A–E): dribble through cones, pass, then sprint and turn out of the grid. Mixed-intensity efforts with ball work.
Two boxes: player dribbles, passes and sprints from A to B, with a defender joining at C. Repeated efforts with opposition.
Penalty-area circuit: players come through ladders, receive, dribble through cones and finish. Players rotate (i, ii).
Multi-station circuit: passing at the mannequins (C), dribbling in the middle (A, B) and sprints. High-intensity mixed efforts.
Cross-shaped circuit: players run in from both sides through ladders (A, B), meet in the centre (C) and curve out to D. Repeated efforts with change of direction.
Two-box circuit: A shuttle runs in a small zone, B a slalom dribble through the far box. Repeated short efforts.
Three lanes: players start at mannequins and do short multi-directional shuttles (A–D). Short high-intensity change-of-direction work.
Pattern with a 1v1 finish: players run i–iv around the grid, then play 1v1 in a small zone. Conditioning with a competitive duel.
Grid with hurdles: players run from A to D via sprints, hurdle hops and a turn at B. Mixed plyometric and running conditioning.
Two mirrored lines in the box: run through ladders, receive, dribble through cones and finish at C. Repeated efforts with ball.
Circuit with hurdles, poles and mannequins: players weave, jump and dribble around the area. Full mixed conditioning circuit.
Multiple rondos in circles on the pitch, each with defenders in the middle; players move between grids on a signal. Possession under pressure with transitions.
Large circle rondo: players around the outside keep the ball from two defenders in the middle. Passing angles, first touch and pressing.
Three rondos in zones with transitions: when the ball is won, players switch to another zone with a long pass. Possession plus switching play.
8v2 circle rondo in a square: eight outside players (including a neutral) keep the ball from two defenders. Quick passing, body shape and splitting passes.
10v2 rondo: ten players on the outside of a large square keep possession against two defenders. High-volume passing with low pressure; good activation rondo.
Wide combination and cross: players combine from A–D down the flank and cross for runners attacking the box against defenders. Crossing, timing of runs and finishing.
Both-flank crossing pattern: pass in from A, overlap or underlap at B and C, then cross for central runners. Wide combinations and finishing.
Combination at the edge of the box: one-two around the defender, then a cross or cut-back from the byline to a runner. Final-third combinations.
Wing play pattern: pass out wide, overlap, cross into the box with runners attacking near and far post. Crossing and movement in the box.
Numbered pattern (1–4) with two teams: wide players deliver crosses as central runners attack set zones. Crossing and finishing with defenders.
Two-goal crossing drill: player drives wide and crosses for runners at one goal while the next sequence starts at the other. High-volume crossing and finishing.
Combination down the right (A and C): pass, overlap and cross for a central runner. Crossing and finishing with timed runs.
Wide players cross from both sides while central players make curved runs into the box. Movement to attack crosses.
